body:
A session on your computer now starts on the newest code from GitHub: at session start (and at the first resume of any role) the kit fetches, and a clean main moves forward by itself. Any other branch or a detached checkout is never moved: its first line says it is behind or stale and what to run. A project whose session start is its own script (Harmonize) now gets the kit's check at session start too.

### What happens at start
SessionStart runs `kit.py fresh` (the trunk fetched, 25 s at most) and its line comes first; `kit.py resume` does the same before anything else, the first time in a session (a mark per session in .kit/run/fresh/). Later resumes look again without fetching and repeat only a line that still asks something.

### The cases
| checkout | what the kit does |
|---|---|
| main, clean, behind | fast-forward to origin/main; one line: how many commits, the newest |
| any other branch with no commit of its own (merged, or a part's new branch), or a detached HEAD | told it is behind, with `git checkout main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` if it is done; never switched (CR-cl53) |
| behind, uncommitted changes | not moved; commit or stash, then the merge to run |
| main with commits not on origin | not moved; `git pull --no-rebase`, then push |
| a branch with its own commits, none for 2+ days while main moved | not moved; stale: merge origin/main or finish it |
| a branch with its own commits, recent | told it is behind |
| a worktree under .claude/worktrees/ | never moved |
| web session | nothing: the clone is fresh |

### A project's own session start
Install, on a Claude Code project whose SessionStart does not run the kit's hook (Harmonize's session-start.sh), adds one line beside it: `python3 -I "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.kit/kit.py" fresh` (it reads the session id from the hook's input). The project's own script is not touched; the line is not added twice, nor where the kit's hook runs.

### Where
`checkout_fresh` and `checkout_fresh_once` in scripts/kit.py, the `fresh` command, kit/hooks/kit_session_start.py, `merge_fresh_line` in install.py, tests/test_checkout_fresh.py.

task:
A session always starts on the newest code from GitHub, in every checkout: the rule "use git" covers the board's data (reconcile at start) and parts (6b69f1e: a part starts on its step's newest work), but not a project's own checkout. ~/harmonize sat on branch agy-board-install from 11-22 while Harmonize's main on GitHub had moved on (0d020efb, 11-24): a session opened there, and the kit's own real-project check, worked on two-day-old code with nothing saying so.

1. At `board` start and at the first resume of any role, the kit fetches origin and says, before anything else, when this checkout is behind its trunk or sits on a branch that is merged or stale (no commit for N days while the trunk moved): one line with what is newer.
2. When the checkout is clean and its branch is the trunk or merged into it, it moves forward by itself (fast-forward, or switch to the trunk); with uncommitted work or commits of its own, it never moves it: it says what to do, and resume names it as the first thing.
3. The same on every platform (a web clone is fresh already: nothing to do there), with a test: a clone behind origin is moved forward at start; one with uncommitted work is only warned.
title: A session always starts on the newest code from GitHub, in every checkout
verdict: Done after the review's redirect: only main moves by itself; a new or merged branch and a detached checkout are told, never switched; Harmonize's session start now runs the check, so its first line says when it is behind.
